# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.33 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.32. Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine. The automated test suite passes on CI runners for Linux x86-64 and arm64, Windows x86-64 and arm64, and macOS (Apple silicon and Intel). **Nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64, and no photo batch was processed there.**

From a tester's notes on pre.31:
- **Fine rotation of the original** before a two-page sheet is cut (window: slider ±20°, number box ±45°; command line: `--sheet-turn DEG`; projects: `turn = DEG`), so a crooked spread gets a vertical gutter. The **Auto** button next to the slider finds the angle. While a turn is set, the original's picture shows the sheet's new axes as thin cyan lines. Hand-drawn zones and guide points, and a dragged cut line, follow the turn.
- **Grid of guide points of any size**: points per line 2-40, lines 1-20 (default still 7 × 5). A double click on the Grid button makes one grid.
- **Bug fixed**: a double click a little beside a guide point put a second point on top of it. No point is added within 16 px of an existing one now.

**Verified**: unit tests and clippy; CI on all jobs. Run by hand on Linux in the window (virtual display): the slider, Undo/Redo of the turn, Auto (found -6.0° on a spread scanned 6° crooked; the pages came out level), the grid button and its size boxes, double clicks beside a point and in the middle of a line. Command line: the same crooked spread, with and without `--sheet-turn`.
**Not verified**: the window on Windows, macOS and arm64; the Auto angle on real photographs or on pages without clear text lines (it then reports no angle); eSCL on a real scanner; the **Dockerfile was never built as an image**; the winget manifest (still pre.28, not validated); the wording of translations by native speakers.

**Known limits**: the picture of the original is not turned (zones are drawn on the sheet as loaded); with perspective correction on, the turn is applied first and the cut line is then read against the corrected sheet (not tried); the other limits of pre.32 stand (large italic heading on a dotted ground can be misread; tables and contents pages read few words; OCR can misread characters such as `@`).
